questions.title: 65. What are React design patterns?
questions.summary:
◦ R^ design patterns = reusable approaches to organizing C^s, state, and UI logic.
◦ Improve reusability, maintainability, and separation of concerns.
questions.answer:
◦ R^ design patterns = established approaches to solving recurring UI architecture problems.
◦ Define how C^s share logic, manage state, and communicate.
◦ Composition → Build complex UI from smaller C^s.
◦ Container/Presentational → Separate data + behavior from UI presentation.
◦ CH^ → Extract reusable stateful logic.
◦ Compound C^ → Coordinate related C^s through shared state/context.
◦ Provider → Share data through Context w/o passing props through every level.
◦ HOC → Wrap a C^ to enhance its behavior.
◦ Render Props → Share behavior through a F() prop.
◦ Choose patterns according to complexity; avoid unnecessary abstraction.
questions.underTheHood:
◦ R^ uses C^ composition to construct its element tree.
◦ Props provide explicit parent → child communication.
◦ Context allows descendants to read a provider's value.
◦ CH^ reuse logic but each C^ call has its own H^ state.
◦ HOCs return enhanced C^ definitions.
◦ Render Props invoke a supplied F() to determine rendered content.
◦ Patterns influence code organization; they do not replace reconciliation or Fiber.
pitfalls: ◦ Design patterns are approaches, not mandatory R^ APIs.
◦ Avoid excessive abstraction for simple C^s.
◦ CH^ share logic, not automatically shared state.
◦ HOCs and Render Props remain valid but CH^ often simplify logic reuse.
questions.recall:
◦ Patterns → Reuse + Separation + Composition.
◦ Container → Logic | Presentational → UI.
◦ CH^ → Logic reuse.
◦ Context/Provider → Shared data.
◦ HOC → Wrap C^.
◦ Render Props → F() prop.

questions.title: 66. What is the Container/Presentational pattern?
questions.summary:
◦ Container C^ → Handles data, state, and behavior.
◦ Presentational C^ → Receives props and renders UI.
questions.answer:
◦ Container/Presentational = R^ pattern separating application logic from UI rendering.
◦ Container C^ → Fetches data, manages state, and handles business logic.
◦ Presentational C^ → Receives data + cb^s through props and describes UI.
◦ Container determines WHAT data and behavior the UI needs.
◦ Presentational determines HOW that data appears.
◦ Improves reuse, testing, and maintainability.
◦ Modern R^ often extracts container logic into CH^s.
questions.underTheHood:
◦ Container C^ executes H^s and prepares props.
◦ Container passes data + event handlers to Presentational C^.
◦ Presentational C^ returns R^ elements from those props.
◦ State changes schedule rendering in the owning C^.
◦ Updated props flow to the Presentational C^.
◦ React.memo may skip its re-r() when props remain unchanged.
◦ Separation is architectural; R^ treats both as ordinary C^s.
pitfalls: ◦ Presentational C^s can still have local UI state.
◦ Container does not have to be a class C^.
◦ Separating every tiny C^ creates unnecessary complexity.
◦ New object/F() props can affect React.memo effectiveness.
◦ CH^s can replace separate containers when appropriate.
followUps: ◦ How do props connect both layers?
questions.recall:
◦ Container → Data + State + Logic.
◦ Presentational → Props + UI.
◦ Flow → Container → Props → Presentational.
◦ Modern alternative → CH^ + UI C^.
